you enjoy intense late game challenge modes

claims.claim: Reviewers note that lighting effects cause poor performance, requiring settings adjustments to run smoothly.

citations.review_text: Classic indie game, but it baffles me how this Indie game from 2017 runs significantly worse than any AAA game from the same period unless I turn off basically every setting related to lighting effects. Even Resident Evil Requiem runs better on my PC than this.

Sorry, but it's a definite AVOID, from me. 
Sure, this looks cute, and the devs are still active, years on, but the core mechanics are terrible.
- No attempt to integrate controllers: They work, but all on-screen prompts are for keyboard presses, so you have no idea what to actually do.
- Camera Control: There is none. The camera is fixed behind you, and can only be zoomed in or out, and only at certain points. A 3D, exploration-based, collectathon platformer without a controllable camera? Yeah, no. This would have been laughed our 20 years ago, now its unforgivable.
- Terrible performance: My machine is far from great, but still WILDLY exceeds the recommended, yet I can barely get 30 FPS out of this, and certainly not consistently.


Just bad. Badly, made, badly thought out, badly delivered.

citations.review_text:
the camera is a bit annoying but it controls really well, besides, this is probably the best 3D platformer you can buy on PC and it will be for a long while thanks to all the mods which are btw, excellently implemented into the game

downloading mods from the workshop is super easy and the game has a dedicated area in the hub to play downloaded levels

I still  haven't played a game with more responsive controls like A hat in time. the camera does show its age but everything else honestly makes up for it. the humour withstood the test of time for sure too.

I should have picked this game up a long time ago.
It's absolutely dripping with personality which made it a joy to play the whole way through. I loved just about everything about the presentation. The music, environments, characters and dialogue all work together very well to create a memorable experience.

The game feels incredible to control, the movement is fluid and gives you just enough options to get to where you want to go without feeling like there's anything missing. There are a couple sore spots where the platforming felt a little awkward or I was fighting with the camera, but none of it detracted from the experience for me. I'd say those moments were the exception rather than the rule.

Overall this is a big recommend for me and it has definitely earned it's place among my favourite games.

Incredible. No, not the game, but how 98% of the Steam community recommends this game. Even praising it as one of the best ever.

Yeah, the characters and setting have charm. That's the best about this game. 
The gameplay mechanics (hats) are already nothing special, not worthy of writing home about.
Control is average at best and the camera ... ugh. The camera alone would result in my thumb going down. 

The levels are a mixed experience. A few are really well made. Others are short and without any challenge or gameplay value. Some others are a pain in the ass, in combination with the bad camera.

Overall: I found little to enjoy and I doubt I'll finish this game.

68/100

It's a collect-a-thon platformer with fun vibes. You'll have a nice time moving through the cartoonish worlds, interacting with the memorable characters, and fighting the cool bosses. It's a chill time.

There are some DIFFICULT challenges to be had in Death Wish, the spike in required skill is crazy high. Good luck if you go this route.

[h1]Rating: 10/10[/h1]
[h2]Fun platformer with a charming art style[/h2]

[h3]The good stuff:[/h3]
+ Really good soundtrack, multiple certified bangers

+ Game oozes with a lot of personality and charm, from the world to the characters and voice acting. It has that cozy, nostalgic feeling to it that reminds you of old 3D platformers like Spyro and Mario Galaxy.

+ The hats are pretty cool and have some fun abilities that allow you to mix around and get creative with it

+ Platforming is fun and level design is top notch. Thoroughly enjoyed basically every level in this game.

+ Death Wish is a great experience for those looking to master the platforming and do some fun challenges (albeit very frustrating and difficult at times too)

[h3]The not-so-good stuff:[/h3]
- I wish the online co-op mode was more developed and actually allowed players to fully play through the campaign together, instead of progress being split amongst the players

[h3]Final thoughts:[/h3]
It's been a while since I played the game so I may have forgotten some parts of the experience. However, to this day a Hat in Time remains one of my favourite platformers, and one thing I do remember is having lots of fun beating it and playing the DLC. I 100% recommend it to anyone who is a big fan of 3D platformers or just wants to play a game that evokes that nostalgic feeling of childhood platformers.

As someone who loves 3D mario games, this game is amazing. although my first playthrough only took 12 hours, I never felt like any of it was wasted. every part of the game kept delivering something unique and I loved seeing everything the game could possibly throw at me. The hats are pretty situational (except for the sprint hat I love you sprint hat) but that can be very easily excused since this design choice feels very intentional on the part of GFB since they've intentionally locked paths in earlier chapters to force you to return to them when you get the rights hats. The story is amazing too, every chapter introduces a new character (except for Alpine Skyline, *boring*) and it makes every chapter feel more fun. you can be an actor for chapter 2 or sell your soul to a ghost for chapter 3. The game's is also very good. The DLC's were also a great adition to the game. Seal the Deal added a whole new chapter although "whole" chapter might be a stretch, theres only 3 act's. You can tell all of the effort went into Death Wish. But death wish is an amazing addition for the people who think the game is too easy at times (including myself) and the bonuses make you go out of your way to do something that makes the level even harder. and the death wish stamps are very varied. there's buffed versions of levels, bosses, levels but with a twist, speedrun levels and even things you have to do in normal levels. And Nyakuza Metro adds my favourite chapter in the game. Nyakuza Metro is another free roam chapter much like Alpine Skyline, but instead of feeling very linear like chapter 4, CHapter 7 actually feels like a free roam chapter (you know, *exploring*?). there are metro passes to collect and the metro feels massive and fun to explore, there are many new cosmetics that are sold in the metro that are a very welcome addition into my inventory and food vendors that let you create food combinations. Nyakuza metro also has alot of stickers wich are very fun to collect. the onli…

if you enjoy this game and are hesitant about the DLCs, i believe Seal the Deal is an absolute must-have. the majority of its negative reviews are just complaints about the difficulty of Death Wish, which is the entire point of Death Wish. Nyakuza Metro is also incredible

citations.review_text: If you like 3D Mario games, you'll like A Hat in Time. It's a perfect tribute and it really captures the essence of games like Sunshine and Galaxy, while adding its own personality and charm. Sure, the load times are a bit extreme. And the camera can be frustrating to deal with, but you can change how it acts in the settings - and I highly recommend doing so - but on the plus side the game is pretty forgiving on platforming challenges to make up for it. Still, the positives far outweigh the flaws. Over all, a great time.

The best 3d platoforming hands down..
 -Story is nice
 -Nice humor, cute af, and appeals literally to everyone
 -Level variety and uniqueness is where it shines for me, bosses, design, art style, i wanted to progress just to see what more they have to show (2 DLCs extend that)
 -Ofc exploration, collectables and replaybility are there
 -Damn even the soundtrack is good, catches the vibe 100%

It literally has everything a 3d platforming game can offer, and it does a pretty good job in all
Now it raised my expectations for the genre..it sticks with you and compares with whatever you have and will play from now on (spyro for instance)
10/10 this is the best game i played this year...i never wanted it to end..wow
(camera movement sometimes is annoying but you get used to it)

You can't prove I spent a good amount of time kicking Mafia guys up the arse because I thought that was one of the missions.

It took me a little while to get into A Hat in Time because I felt somewhat overwhelmed by the huge size of the opening world. But then I really started to get into it and this is easily one of the greatest 3D platformers I've ever played.

Camera eccentricities aside (wouldn't be a 3D platformer without them), the variety in gameplay, worlds and settings is as impressive as the gameplay is constantly challenging and entertaining. The characters are beautifully written, there's loads of moments of humour, and the ending is quite sweet too. Loved this.

Not making a sequel is insanity though.

Amazing game and I believe one of the few things I backed where I don't feel disappointed. Now at the late stage of its lifecycle, it has been kitted out with plenty of community and modding tools as well as streamlining our ability to share them with one another. citations.review_text:
One of my favorite platformers!!

I love how this game is presented as this silly little game that doesn't take itself seriously. We need more games like this.

All the characters are amazingly made and I like them a lot!!!

The main story gameplay is simple and fairly easy, but there is Death Wish if you want an actual challenge.

I love the modding community so much and doing Challenge Roads too.

Also in the Vanessa's Curse DLC, the servers are a ghost town. So when you actually find some people to play with, it's so much fun.

This is a literal must-play for any 3D platforming fan. Controls, music, theming, story, dialogue, and more are all excellent. Additionally, the two main DLC expansions (Seal the Deal and Nyakuza Metro) are exceptional. If you are considering buying this game, you should definitely buy those two alongside it for your first playthrough. There is admittedly not much reason to buy Vanessa's Curse as it's a dead online mode.

My only real grievances are: 
1) The game is not super well-optimized and has a tendency to run poorly, crash, or massively stutter on certain systems depending on your settings. You may have to edit the settings.ini file manually just to get the game to load.
2) Even after playing nearly 150hrs, the camera is a little tough to get used to. It fights REALLY hard and makes it so you essentially have to do some (totally optional) tricks blind because the camera is determined to zoom in and focus on like, the wall or a rock or something.

For those that dont want to read, TLDR: This game is fun, and will challenge you if you want to fully 100% this game. Recommended to pickup when it goes on sale, and best experienced with the dlc. Additionally, it has a decently sized modding community, if that is your cup of tea. Co-op is fun, but requires mods for the best experience if you choose to use the online party feature.

I wanted to hold off on writing a review until I had fully completed the entire game. As of writing this, I had just gotten the final achievement, and the last thing needed to fully complete my save file.
This game takes inspiration for alot of collect-a-thons like Banjo & Kazooie, but has the gameplay style mostly matching games like Super Mario Sunshine/Galaxy.  The story I personally enjoyed, and the gamplay is pretty solid. I found the base game to be easy myself, but some people can find the game tough. If you find the game to be too easy, the game will not hold back any punches if you aim for 110% completion.

The base game holds up well on its own, but the DLC I think is what makes the game much more enjoyable. Ranging from an entire challenge mode, new worlds/levels, and player customization. The creator dlc, despite what people say, can be fun. But getting a decently match is hard these days, due to a smaller player base than when that dlc launched. Dedicated online parties exist just for this side experience though. The challenge mode imo is worth picking up. Most of my time with this game was trying to fully complete it. along the way, it taught me things I never knew about the game, and helped me get better at other games too.

The game also features a pretty extensive list of community made levels, customizations, qol, almost anything TBH. This type of stuff I found myself enjoying, but the quality can vary ALOT and its all depending on your personal preference.

The multiplayer in this game is also a fun experience. The splitscreen co-op will take some time to get …

citations.review_text: I've played this game consistently for 10 years and not once did I realize I haven't written a review for it until now. This is one of my favorite games of all time. Everything about it is perfect: the level design, tight controls, masterfully created music, and memorable characters work in tandem to make the perfect love letter to the 3D platformer genre. This, "Cute as Heck 3D platformer" is a blast start to finish and doesn't miss ONCE throughout the entire game. It's a rare example of a kickstarter game gone right. And this is all just for the BASE GAME. The two campaign DLCs take the game to the next level BOTH TIMES. I fondly remember impatiently sitting in my seat at school because it was DLC day and I got to play NEW Hat in Time content when I got home, and it was always worth the wait! Gears for Breakfast simply didn't miss when developing this game. Nearly 10 years after release I haven't run out of things to do because of the modding support. W devs, W game, W community, W kid with the hat.

This game genuinely is one of the best if not the best 3d platformer I have played in my entire life. Absolutely hilarious and fun to follow story, and some of the most loveable characters with soul and love put into each animation and voice line. The gameplay with each unique hats add to different puzzles the more you progress and although collectibles aren't necessary, they are beyond fun to collect compared to other games. The community has such a strong commitment and love to this game and has created some amazing levels, skins, hats, etc. There are custom levels that are super fun to play alongside faithful recreations of levels from other platformers. The DLC's in this game is full of so much love despite one of them being short, and the challenge mode the game provides was one of the most enjoyable challenge roads I've played. The little details from the easter eggs, to hidden little areas inside the ship are very fun to discover as they require following riddles and game tech to reach them. Also any game that supports trans rights is a plus in my book and finding the trans flag in the DLC was a very welcome thing to see. The multiplayer in this game is beyond fun as it doesn't "force" you into a lobby with other people and one person controls what level you go to. Rather you enter a lobby code in the ship and you can just play the game *alongside* your friends, with being able to do whatever levels while the other does one, and challenging each other to little challenges when entering levels together. If you are looking for an extremely fun game to pass the time either alone or with people you love I HIGHLY recommend this gem of a game.

Awesome vidyagame. Very fun world to explore & many things to collect, many many adorable cosmetics that fit the 2 precious protagonists perfectly. Game quality varies across locations and at times feels a bit cobbled-together but i find it incredibly charming and most people don't seem to mind it much either. The plot is questionable but the gameplay and character make up for it. 

Amazing compatibility with mods, many custom levels and cosmetics. DLCs are very high quality (except Death Wish) and fit with the base game well, I'm a huge fan of Nyakuza Metro. (Smugdance)

1) The game is not super well-optimized and has a tendency to run poorly, crash, or massively stutter on certain systems depending on your settings. You may have to edit the settings.ini file manually just to get the game to load.
2) Even after playing nearly 150hrs, the camera is a little tough to get used to. It fights REALLY hard and makes it so you essentially have to do some (totally optional) tricks blind because the camera is determined to zoom in and focus on like, the wall or a rock or something.

I'm sure someone else has already done a much better job of going into some sort of full breakdown for this gem of a game. I'm not going to do that. Instead, I'm just going to talk about how this game made me feel and who I think it's for.

A Hat in Time is a game that reminded me of what games are really all about- or at least what they used to be about. I felt nostalgia and joy for something I've been yearning for and never even realized it was missing. What am I talking about? It's going to sound corny, but love. Love for video games shared by both the developers and their players. The love needed to make something beautiful and artistic and to want to create something beyond just a product that makes money. It made me miss every game I had growing up that felt like a polished full experience from the moment I started. An adventure that pulls me in with its charm, music, and visuals even if it isn't using the latest and greatest textures and hyper realistic worlds we see in more modern games- games that often feel incomplete or empty despite these visual advances. AHIT pays tribute to (and makes one feel dejavu for) some of the greatest 3D platformers ever made such as Banjo Kajooie, Spyro, Jack & Daxter, Ratchet and Clank, Psychonauts, Mario Sunshine & Mario Odyssey. Just to name a few. It reminds me of these legendary classics but while being completely its own game at the same time. It reminds of why I loved those games and even makes improves on the frustrating limitations of those games as it has many impactful QoL improvements you didn't have before. There are tons of options in the game that can impact the difficulty of levels or be more accessible, there is a strong modding community and the game was clearly built with modding and speed running in mind from the ground up (but if you aren't about those things, then you'll enjoy the game all the same). The game supports local co-op as well as large online groups with the DLCs they've added.

citations.review_text:
This is a literal must-play for any 3D platforming fan. Controls, music, theming, story, dialogue, and more are all excellent. Additionally, the two main DLC expansions (Seal the Deal and Nyakuza Metro) are exceptional. If you are considering buying this game, you should definitely buy those two alongside it for your first playthrough. There is admittedly not much reason to buy Vanessa's Curse as it's a dead online mode.

My only real grievances are: 
1) The game is not super well-optimized and has a tendency to run poorly, crash, or massively stutter on certain systems depending on your settings. You may have to edit the settings.ini file manually just to get the game to load.
2) Even after playing nearly 150hrs, the camera is a little tough to get used to. It fights REALLY hard and makes it so you essentially have to do some (totally optional) tricks blind because the camera is determined to zoom in and focus on like, the wall or a rock or something.

On a casual level, this is a wonderful 3D platformer with some very tight level design, loads of things to collect, and a charming style. It's goofy in a way that I like. 
It does run on Unreal Engine 3, and is a bit hard on your system to run for it's cartoony/simple visual style, but I can look past this because it's far from the hardest game in the world to run. 
The hats in the game are an okay tool in a normal play-through, but you really do end up using just the sprint hat most of the time, with certain set-pieces that encourage you to use the other hats from time to time. 
It also has a pretty good co-op mode, and with online party you can see other players in passing in levels and emote to one another. 
I think the game really shines as a relatively easy to get into speedrun. This is where the movement mechanics and the hats are at their best, because there's a lot of tech you can take advantage of. The Ice hat, which you normally use to launch yourself on designated launchpads, can be used to gain large amounts of momentum on sloped platforms to launch yourself, for example. 
Workshop support means access to some good resources for practicing as well. 
I do highly recommend this game whether you intend to play it casually or speedrun, or both.

I bought this game when it first came out, and did all the achievements at the time, but the dlcs started crashing my game so now with a new laptop I was finally able to truly finish it. I really love this game, there's some janky things in it, my laptop did start to overheat on Snatcher Ex with all the lasers and such even though it can run Elden Ring just fine, and there are a few frustrating bugs here and there. But this is just such a good and fun game. The movement feels so good, the stages are all so fun to traverse, every track is such a banger, the harder levels in seal the deal feel so good to complete. I didn't play any of the online modes but I can only assume it's a great time as well. I really love this game, it is really good, it's just a real great ride begining to end.
